An update to n2den, the experimental Nintendo Switch 2 recompulator built on Eden.

n2den runs decrypted dumps of games you own. It contains no decryption code, does not use console keys, and includes no games.

## Downloads

| Package | What it is |
|---|---|
| `n2Den-v1.0.1-windows-x64-pgo.zip` | **Recommended.** Built with clang, ThinLTO and a profile trained on gameplay: the faster build. The command-line `n2Den-cli.exe` is only in the MSVC package. |
| `n2Den-v1.0.1-windows-x64.zip` | The same source built with MSVC, like the test builds. Use it if the PGO build misbehaves on your machine. |
| `*-symbols.zip` | Debug symbols for crash reports. Not needed to play. |

Windows x64 with a Vulkan GPU. Extract into a new folder; create an empty `user` folder beside `n2Den.exe` for portable mode. You can extract over 1.0.0 or keep both side by side.

## What's new since 1.0.0

### New games

- **Donkey Kong Bananza** now reaches the first level with a correct picture on both graphics backends.
- **Orbitals Deluxe Edition** boots to its title screen with the right picture and sound, plays its opening movie, and goes in-game (slowly) on NVN-HLE.
- **Xenoblade Chronicles 2 – Nintendo Switch 2 Edition** now boots and runs its intro and title screen. The intro's colours are correct, but the 3D scene does not reach the screen yet (only the title text and menus show, over black).

### Speed

- Donkey Kong Bananza on NVN-HLE runs more than 500% faster than in the first builds that reached its levels, and on the emulated GPU about 50% faster. Both are still below full speed.
- Less work per frame on the NVN-HLE backend: image views and framebuffers are now reused instead of being recreated, which lowers CPU use in busy scenes.
- Orbitals' gameplay no longer spends most of its time creating the same buffer views over and over, and its opening movie no longer drops to a crawl.

### Fixes

- Sound now plays in games that mix their audio through the Switch 2's own sound mixer (Orbitals was silent before).
- Games that keep their own record of displayed frames no longer freeze after a few seconds.
- Fixed a graphics device loss when a Donkey Kong Bananza level loads.
- Fixed a black floor in Donkey Kong Bananza on the emulated GPU.
- Fixed wrong colours in games that build their own colour-grading tables (Xenoblade Chronicles 2's intro looked green and red).
- Games that reserve very large amounts of memory address space at start-up no longer crash at boot.
- Games packed as a single program in a `.nup` container can now read their shared game data.
- Fixed pink and black screens in Unreal Engine games caused by several texture-handling gaps.
- More NVN graphics functions are handled on NVN-HLE, so fewer games stop on a missing one. Thanks to ScarletNX, whose handlers several of these were ported from.
- A memory leak that let some games grow until the system ran out of RAM is now capped.
- Many smaller stability fixes in the GPU synchronisation and shader translation code.

### Options

- A new built-in add-on, "Single-interval vsync for Donkey Kong Bananza", in that game's settings.

## Tested games

| Game | Emulated GPU | NVN-HLE (Vulkan) |
|---|---|---|
| The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time (Switch 2) | In-game | In-game |
| Fire Emblem: Fortune's Weave | In-game | In-game |
| Fast Fusion | Playable | Playable |
| Kirby and the Forgotten Land – Nintendo Switch 2 Edition + Star-Crossed World | Playable | Playable |
| Donkey Kong Bananza | In-game | In-game |
| Orbitals Deluxe Edition | Not usable | In-game, slow |
| Xenoblade Chronicles 2 – Nintendo Switch 2 Edition | Not tested | Boots |
| Nintendo Switch Sports Resort | Not tested | Boots |
| Mario Kart World | Not tested | Unstable |

Details and known issues per game: [docs/GameProgress.md](https://github.com/Duck912/n2den/blob/main/docs/GameProgress.md). Games not in the table have not been tested.

## Known issues

- Expect missing graphics and crashes: this is a development release.
- Xenoblade Chronicles 2 shows only its menus over a black background, and games in large `.nup` containers take a while to load because their data is unpacked at every start.
- The first time a new area or effect appears there is a short stutter while its shaders build; later runs reuse the cache.
- Mario Kart World can run out of system RAM after several minutes and is not recommended for play.
- Only Windows is supported for now.

## Reporting problems

Open an issue with `user\log\eden_log.txt` (or `%APPDATA%\eden\log\eden_log.txt`), taken right after the problem, plus your GPU and driver version.
